title: Water and the chemistry of life
titleAsPrinted: Water and the Chemistry of Life

examBlueprint.tests: B1.1 to B1.5, two items each
Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B1.4 reading (Miller-Urey)

standards.title: Atoms, bonding, and polarity
standards.description: How atoms are built, how electron configuration determines how an atom bonds, and how electronegativity differences make some molecules, like water, polar.
iCan: I can describe the structure of H, C, N, and O (protons, neutrons, electrons in shells) and draw accurate Bohr models.
I can explain how the number of valence electrons determines how many bonds an atom can form, and I can distinguish isotopes from ions.
I can correctly tell apart nonpolar covalent, polar covalent, ionic, and hydrogen bonds.
I can use electronegativity to explain why water is polar and how hydrogen bonds form between water molecules.

standards.title: Water's emergent properties
standards.description: All six emergent properties of water at the molecular level, each connected to something that matters in biology or ecology.
iCan: I can explain all six properties (cohesion, adhesion, specific heat, evaporative cooling, solvent behavior, ice density) using hydrogen-bond reasoning at the molecular level.
I can connect each property to a biological or ecological function.
My lab records are complete, legible, and clearly separate observation from inference.

exam.examItems: MC Q1, Q4; SA 12; Part 3 CER; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: pH, acids, bases, and buffers
standards.description: The pH scale as a logarithmic measure of hydrogen ion concentration, the difference between acids and bases, and how buffers maintain stable pH.
iCan: I can explain the pH scale as a log scale based on hydrogen ion concentration [H+].
I can distinguish strong from weak acids by how completely they dissociate.
I can describe how the bicarbonate / carbonic acid buffer resists pH change and explain why blood pH must stay within a narrow range.

standards.title: Carbon chemistry, functional groups, and polymers
standards.titleAsPrinted: Carbon Chemistry, Functional Groups, and Polymers
standards.description: Why carbon's four bonds make structural diversity possible, the major functional groups, what the Miller-Urey experiment did and did not show, and how cells build and break polymers from monomers.
iCan: I can explain why carbon's four bonds allow structural diversity.
I can identify the hydroxyl, carboxyl, amino, and phosphate groups and describe their key properties.
I can explain what the Miller-Urey experiment demonstrated and what it did not prove.
I can define monomer and polymer, name the four macromolecule classes, and explain dehydration synthesis and hydrolysis.

exam.examItems: MC Q7, Q8; SA 15, 16 (Part 5 passage also draws on this standard)

standards.title: Macromolecule structure determines function
standards.description: For each of the four macromolecule classes (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids), how its structure gives rise to its function.
